children: Grades were little changed on Thursday, dealers said, as markets weighed the risk to global supply amid escalating attacks by Yemen's Houthis on Saudi Arabian oil infrastructure.

Yemen's Houthis said on Thursday they attacked Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura oil refinery, Rabigh oil refinery and an Aramco facility in Abqaiq. There was no immediate confirmation from Saudi Arabia on the Houthi statement.

Earlier, US Vice President JD Vance sought to revive peace negotiations by sending a letter to Mohsen Rezaei, the head of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday, citing US officials and people familiar with the matter.
Meanwhile, the US military's senior officer overseeing the Middle East met US President
at the White House on Thursday to outline military options in Iran, the Wall Street Journal reported, citing US officials and other people with direct knowledge of the meeting.

Separately, Saudi Arabia is expected to keep its official selling prices for crude oil bound for Asia at a six-year low in December, a Reuters survey showed, as ample Middle East supplies and weaker spot market premiums weighed. Low prices for Middle East crude could mean lower demand for US oil in Asia.
Light Louisiana Sweet (WTC-LLS) for December delivery eased 5 cents to a midpoint of a $3.00 premium and was seen bid and offered between a $2.00 and $4.00 a barrel premium to US crude futures
Mars Sour (WTC-MRS) eased 10 cents to a midpoint of a $1.90 premium and was seen bid and offered between a $1.70 and $2.10 a barrel premium to US crude futures
WTI Midland (WTC-WTM) eased 5 cents to a midpoint of a 40-cent premium and was seen bid and offered between a 20-cent and 60-cent a barrel premium to US crude futures
West Texas Sour (WTC-WTS) eased 15 cents to a midpoint of a $1.50 discount and was seen bid and offered between a $1.75 and $1.25 a barrel discount to US crude futures
WTI at East Houston (WTC-MEH), also known as MEH, traded between a 50-cent and 90-cent a barrel premium to US crude futures
were down 44 cents to $114.88 a barrel on Thursday​
futures fell 78 cents to $102.00 a barrel on Thursday​
The Brent/WTI spread (WTCLc1-LCOc1) widened to last trade at minus $12.88, after hitting a high of minus $12.32 and a low of minus $13.44
